tools.name: list_places
tools.description: The places that have upcoming quantum computing events: continents, countries, states where a country is searched by state, and cities, each with its number of events. Use the codes or names it returns as filters for list_events.

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: Upcoming quantum computing events, soonest first, as summaries. Every filter is optional and they combine. Events are run by their own organisers; QDev checks each against its organiser's page. At most 50 a call; pass nextCursor back as cursor for more.

tools.name: get_event
tools.description: One event in full: dates, time zone, venue and place, summary, what is not yet settled, deadlines, the organiser's page, its page on quantumdev.io, and the date QDev last checked it.

tools.name: get_event_calendar
tools.description: One event as an iCalendar (.ics) file, ready to add to a calendar. Returns the file's name, media type and text.

tools.name: list_qpus
tools.description: The quantum computers reachable through the cloud that QDev's directory lists, with simulators and retired machines: each one's provider, technology, qubit count, region and status. A status is the provider's own word as of the time in asOf; say "as of" that time, since it can change by the minute.

tools.name: get_qpu
tools.description: One machine in full: what it is, its status with the time it was read and what that status means, its qubit count, how its qubits connect, its native operations, the hours it runs work and when they next open or close, what is waiting in its queues, its region and place, the provider's own summary a

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: Every public page and blog post on quantumdev.io: id, title, address, description and date. Use get_document for the text of one.

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: One page or blog post of quantumdev.io as markdown, with its title, address and date. Pages include the home page (what QDev is and its products), the privacy policy and the terms.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the events, the quantum computers, the pages and the blog posts of quantumdev.io by text. Returns matching results, best first, each with an id to pass to fetch.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: The full text of one search result, by its id: an event written out with its dates, place, deadlines and links, a quantum computer written out with its status and facts, or a page or post as markdown.

tools.name: join_email_list
tools.description: Starts a sign-up to QDev's email list for a person who asked to join. QDev emails that address a confirmation link, and the address joins the list only when its owner opens the email and presses Confirm. findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "join_email_list" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Starts a sign-up to QDev's email list for a person who asked to join. QDev emails that address a confirmation link, and the address joins the list only when its…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_documents, get_document, search, fetch, join_email_list · Private data: get_event_calendar, list_documents, get_document · Public sink: list_documents, get_document, fetch, join_email_list · Destructive: list_events.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_documents, get_document, search, fetch, join_email_list · Private data: get_event_calendar, list_documents, get_document · Public sink: list_documents, get_document, fetch, join_email_list · Destructive: list_events

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Search the events, pages and blog posts of quantumdev.io by text. Returns matching results, best first, each with an id to pass to fetch." → after: "Search the events, the quantum computers, the pages and the blog posts of quantumdev.io by text. Returns matching results, best first, each with an id to pass to fetch."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
